newsitem.title: RUSSIA: AGROKHLEB - Russia harvest estimate cut - 69.5 mln T.
newsitem.headline: AGROKHLEB - Russia harvest estimate cut - 69.5 mln T.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from the Agrokhleb Report, published by SovEcon Ltd, an independent research organisation specialising in agricultural production and trade in the former Soviet Union.
SOVECON CUTS FORECAST FOR RUSSIAN GRAIN HARVEST BY 2.5 MILLION TONNES TO 69.5 MILLION TONNES

MOSCOW, Aug 28 - In most regions, yields continue to decline with the harvest progress. The 1996 average grain yields are now forecast at about 1.3 tonne per ha (cleaned weight), compared to 1.16 tonne per ha last year.

Due to lower yields in west and East Siberia at the beginning of the harvest campaign, total grain output in these regions have revised downwards by 1.2 million tonnes for West Siberia and nearly 0.4 million tonnes for East Siberia. Moreover, if there are delays in harvesting, total grain output for these regions is likely to be revised down further.
Forecasts for other regions have not been much changed except for Central and Central-Chernozem regions, where dry weather has reduced yields.

As a result, Russia's total grain output in 1996 has been revised downwards by about 2.5 million tonnes to 68-72 million tonnes. It is about 11 pct up on the drought-affected harvest last year, but it will be the third lowest output in the last three decades.
